goalInOwnWords: Build a line that turns scrap into the most valuable thing it can (ingots), fill each shift's money order to earn stars (an order is a money target for one shift, and filling it makes every price rise 25% of the starting price), and finish with more total money than Sal.
stoppedWhere: Shift 6 retry (Try again from shift 6) on today's yard: the forecast was still $474 short of the $5,820 order and could not beat my $17,796 best, so I chose Menu, Save and go home, then the feedback form.
stoppedWhy: I had my answer: 5 of 6 orders, $132 ahead of Sal, and the forecast said the retry could not reach three stars. I could not find the last 9 ingots without a pencil and it was no longer lunch. I would come back and replay this yard from shift 1 using the next-shift previews and the leftover parts I wasted.

stuck.where: Shift 2 of the real yard, building the second feed
stuck.what: The forecast stayed flat at $1,080 while I placed the new hopper and crusher, and I thought the card did nothing. The crusher was also flagged as leading nowhere when I fed it into the side of the splitter.
stuck.gotOutHow: Read the small grey note that it pays when the last piece is in, then moved the hopper and crusher so the crusher fed the first furnace from the side; the forecast jumped to $1,470.

stuck.where: Shifts 5 and 6, needing the last two orders
stuck.what: A card with nothing to improve (the game said no spot pays more) left me with three splitters, a furnace and a dock on the shelf, and I did not realise they were reusable until the retry.
stuck.gotOutHow: Did not fully get out: on the retry I rebuilt with the shelf parts but the forecast still came out $474 short of the last order.

confused: How to play and the job card say every price goes up 25% but not whether of the current price or the starting one; I assumed it compounds and my plan was wrong until a furnace card showed ingots at $36.
The forecast stays at the old number until the last piece of a card is down, so the first two pieces seem to do nothing; the note explaining this is small and grey.
Lesson 1 lists Crusher and Furnace as needed, yet Sal says 'Line closed' for a belt from hopper to dock, which looked contradictory.
I only learned a shift is 80 seconds from the 'held you back for 63 of 80 seconds' line, never from a rule.
Spare parts from a card that cannot improve the line (I took a Furnace card with no spot that pays more) pile up on the shelf with no hint they can be used later.
annoyed: No leaderboard in the test version; beating a daily board is what keeps me coming back to my other puzzles.
Picking a card that does nothing felt like a wasted turn, and New offers costs $40.
Placing and rearranging needs many single drags; making a three-furnace layout took nine or ten actions.
Missing the third star by about 9 ingots with no cheap way to find them.
pleased: Every shift ends with an itemised receipt like '36 x ingot @ $24 = $864' that adds up to the dollar, including belt costs and spare sales.
The 'This shift will pay $X' forecast was exactly right every time and shows how short of the order I am before I start.
'What held you back' names the slow machine and the seconds lost, and the red tag sits on the machine itself.
The next shift's offers are shown ahead, so I can plan two moves out.
Sal as a running target: 'You're $30 behind Sal', then '$516 ahead of Sal'.
Dragging a placed piece to move it, and refusals that explain themselves (the dashed truck spot).
'One more order for three stars' plus 'Try again from shift 6'.
bestMoment: Shift 2 of the real yard: I wired the second crusher into the first furnace myself, the forecast jumped from $1,080 to $1,470, and the result matched exactly.
worstMoment: Seeing the retry of shift 6 still $474 short of the last order after rebuilding the whole layout, and not being able to find the last nine ingots.
oneChange: Put a daily leaderboard back and say in the rules that each filled order adds 25% of the starting price; with those two, and a way to replay a yard from shift 1, I would play every day.
